10.1002_anie.1678852: Self‐assembled monolayers (SAMs) have emerged as efficient hole‐transporting materials for inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs). However, the synergistic design of SAMs that simultaneously optimizes electronic structure, molecular packing, perovskite crystallization, and interfacial contact remains underexplored, and the development of new SAMs is often impeded by complex synthetic routes. Herein, we developed an asymmetric [1]benzothieno[3,2‐b]indole (BTI) core via a concise Fischer indole synthesis. From this core, three SAMs are obtained by sequentially introducing substituents with electron‐donating to electron‐withdrawing characteristics. As the electron‐withdrawing ability of the substituents increases, the SAMs exhibited progressively enhanced electron delocalization, improved energy‐level alignment with perovskite, and preserved long‐range ordered molecular packing. The improved SAMs film quality enables them to act as effective templating layers for perovskite deposition, directing perovskite crystallization, improving buried interfacial contact, and suppressing interfacial nonradiative recombination. Consequently, the inverted PSCs with F‐4PABTI deliver a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 26.76%, a high open‐circuit voltage ( V OC ) of 1.203 V, and markedly improved operational stability. Notably, the large area device (1 cm 2 ), module (655.2 cm 2 ), and wide‐bandgap device (1.84 eV) achieve excellent PCEs of 25.38%, 20.59%, and 17.87%, respectively. This work offers a rational molecular design strategy for advancing high‐performance and stable PSCs.
10.1016_j.ijdrr.2026.106353: Flood-prone urban slums face rising climate risks, yet conventional flood management often fails to account for the social and ecological dynamics that shape resilience. This study examines how flood characteristics and social–ecological interactions influence flood risk management (FRM) in two Indonesian cities: Bima and Pontianak. Using an exploratory mixed-methods design, we combine hydrological and hydraulic modelling (HEC-HMS and HEC-RAS), household surveys, and 39 interviews with residents and local authorities. Cognitive mapping was used to visualize interaction networks and analyze their structural patterns. Findings show that local flood perceptions, shaped by lived experience rather than technical metrics, influence how communities assess and respond to flood risks. In some cases, these perceptions diverge from the heightened risk identified through modelling, particularly where frequent low-level inundation leads to risk normalization. In Bima, recent flash floods have generated collective urgency and coordinated early warnings, while in Pontianak, more gradual and shallow events foster individualized coping. These contrasting dynamics affect the coherence between community practices and formal planning. We argue that effective FRM must engage with local knowledge and its divergence from technical assessments to better support sustained resilience.
10.1016_j.ijhydene.2026.158199: Proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) requires efficient platinum group metal (PGM)-free catalysts for green hydrogen production. Herein, we present a workflow for evaluating hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) catalysts under application relevant PEMWE conditions using pentlandites as model compounds. Among the investigated materials, Co 6 . 75 Ni 2 . 25 S 8 exhibited the best device-level performance, delivering competitive cell voltages (2.03 V at 1 A cm −2 ) and stable hydrogen production. Our post-mortem workflow using ICP-OES, SEM/EDX, PXRD and XPS revealed increased catalyst dissolution and Co/Ni migration into the membrane compared to Pt. Distribution of relaxation times (DRT) analysis identified the kinetic, transport and degradation processes governing cell operation. Continuous operation appeared beneficial compared to intermittent operation regarding degradation. The proposed workflow distinguishes electrochemical performance from structural stability via cross-validation of orthogonal methods, providing a decision framework for assessing the industrial applicability of emerging PGM-free HER catalysts and guiding protocol development and further optimization for durable PEMWE operation.
10.1016_j.seppur.2026.139489: Forward osmosis (FO) has shown high dye rejection in textile applications, but many studies still treat it as an end-of-pipe step and rely on synthetic feeds, leaving limited evidence on its practical integration into dyeing operations using real industrial baths. In this study, FO was evaluated as an in-process circular strategy to reconcentrate real industrial dyeing baths and enable reuse of both concentrated baths and recovered water. By combining factorial optimization, long-term reconcentration of three industrial dyeing baths, membrane-fingerprint analysis, and re-dyeing validation, this work advances beyond previous studies by assessing not only dye rejection or water recovery, but also the operational feasibility and reuse potential of FO-retained dye baths. A factorial design assessed the effects of draw-solution (DS) concentration (NaCl, 1–5 mol/L) and recirculation velocities (20–60 cm/s). Flux ranged from 4.15 to 5.58 L·m −2 ·h −1 , with a strong improvement when DS increased from 1 to 3 mol/L, while gains were limited at 5 mol/L due to polarization and reverse salt diffusion. Response-surface optimization targeting concentration factor (CF) selected 3 mol/L NaCl, FS velocity 20 cm/s, and DS velocity 40 cm/s for long-term tests with three real dyeing baths (black, navy, royal). Average fluxes were 7.09, 8.01, and 10.40 L·m −2 ·h −1 , with normalized flux declines of 6%, 6%, and 19% over 2880 min. Overall water recovery in the long-term reconcentration runs reached up to 88% and the performance losses were governed predominantly by osmotic effects (reverse NaCl diffusion and feed salinity build-up), rather than by severe fouling-driven resistance. UV–Vis monitoring showed bath-dependent reconcentration (CF = 2.13 black, 1.20 navy, 2.28 royal). Complementary analysis using EEM suggested stronger interaction/deposition for the black bath, whereas royal and navy membranes remained close to pristine fingerprints. Re -dyeing tests confirmed that FO retentates remained usable for dyeing, supporting their use as value streams through blending and recipe adjustment. Long-term tests with DS replenishment showed incomplete flux recovery due to salinity build-up, with Js/Jw of 6.32–12.58 g·L −1 , highlighting the need to balance reuse benefits and salt carryover in NaCl-driven FO.
